jute_dsl_spec.description: Jute is a JSON/YAML-based template language for data transformation. Templates are JSON/YAML documents where string values starting with '$ ' are evaluated as expressions against an input scope (data context). Objects with special directive keys ($if, $map, etc.) control flow and iteration. The result is a new JSON document with all expressions resolved.

expression_syntax.overview: Expressions are string values prefixed with '$ ' (dollar sign + space). They are evaluated against the current scope — the input data plus any variables introduced by directives like $let or $map.

path_navigation.description: Dot-separated path to traverse nested objects. Returns the value at that path, or null if any segment is missing.

array_indexing.description: Access array elements by zero-based index. Negative indices count from the end (-1 = last element).

wildcards.description: Single wildcard '*' expands over all elements of an array or all values of an object at that level, returning an array of results.

deep_wildcards.description: Double wildcard '**' recursively traverses all nested structures, collecting all values for the specified field at any depth.

examples.description: Collect all prices from any depth

predicates.description: Filter elements where the condition is true. Inside the predicate, 'this' refers to the current element being tested. Variables from the outer scope are also accessible.

examples.description: Filter books cheaper than 10
Filter using outer scope variable

dynamic_paths.description: Use a parenthesized expression as a dynamic path component. The expression is evaluated and its result is used as the key/index.

root_reference.description: The '@' symbol refers to the root of the current scope. Useful when you need to reference the entire input or when inside a directive that has shadowed outer variables.

pipe_operator.description: Pipeline operator passes the left-hand value as the first argument to the right-hand function. Enables readable left-to-right data transformation chains.

function_call_in_path.description: Function call results can be used as path heads, allowing further path navigation on the return value.

string_literals.description: String literals can be expressed with single or double quotes inside expressions.

null_comparison.description: Null is a first-class value. Comparing with null works as expected. Note: null is distinct from the string 'null'.

numeric_string_keys.description: When accessing a map with numeric string keys, the numeric path component is tried as a string key on maps. On arrays, it's used as an index.

notes: Operator precedence follows standard mathematical conventions.
The + operator on strings performs concatenation: $ "hello, " + name
Equality is strict: $ true = "True" evaluates to false.
Arithmetic expressions follow standard precedence: $ 2 + 3 * 3 yields 11 (not 15).

$if.description: Conditional evaluation. Evaluates a condition and returns one of two branches.

parameters.$if: Expression that evaluates to a truthy/falsy value
parameters.$then: Value returned when condition is true (full form)
parameters.$else: Value returned when condition is false (full form, optional — defaults to null)

behavior: Full form: returns $then if condition is truthy, $else otherwise (null if no $else).
Short form (no $then/$else): returns the object without the $if key when true, null when false.
Condition is strict: only false and null are falsy. 0 and empty string are truthy.

examples.description: Full form with $then and $else
Returns null when condition is false and no $else
Short form returns object without $if when true
Short form returns null when false
Boolean comparison is strict (true != "True")

$map.description: Iterate over an array or object, evaluating $body for each element. Returns an array of results.

parameters.$map: Expression evaluating to an array or object to iterate over
parameters.$as: Variable name (string) or [item, index] pair (array) to bind each element
parameters.$body: Template evaluated for each element; the bound variable is added to scope

behavior: For arrays: each element is bound to the $as variable.
For arrays with index: use $as: [item, idx] to get both element and zero-based index.
For objects: each entry is bound as {key: <key>, value: <value>}.

examples.description: Map over array with greeting
Map with index binding
Map over object yields key/value pairs

$reduce.description: Reduce/fold an array or object into a single accumulated value.

parameters.$reduce: Expression evaluating to an array or object
parameters.$start: Initial value for the accumulator (also accepted as $from)
parameters.$body: Expression evaluated for each element; must produce the next accumulator value

behavior: Iterates over the collection, threading the accumulator through each step.
For objects: each item is bound as {key: <key>, value: <value>}.

examples.description: Concatenate names with separator
Flatten object values into single array

$let.description: Introduce local variables into scope, then evaluate $body with the extended scope.

parameters.$let: Object of {name: expression} bindings, or array of single-key objects for ordered evaluation
parameters.$body: Template evaluated with the new variables in scope

behavior: Object form: all bindings are evaluated with access to the original scope.
Array form: bindings are evaluated in order; later bindings can reference earlier ones.
Existing scope variables remain accessible in $body alongside new bindings.

examples.description: Object-style variable binding
Array-style sequential binding with chained computation

$fn.description: Define a reusable function that can be called from expressions or via $call.

parameters.$body: Template evaluated when the function is called, with parameters in scope
parameters.$name: Optional. Assigns a name to the function for recursive self-reference.

behavior: Returns a callable function value. Typically assigned via $let, then invoked in expressions.
Use $name to enable recursion — the function can call itself by that name.

examples.description: Define and call a simple function
Closure — inner function accesses outer scope
Recursive function (fibonacci)

$call.description: Invoke a function (built-in or user-defined) with an array of arguments.

parameters.$call: Function name (string) — looks up in current scope first, then built-in functions
parameters.$args: Array of arguments, or an expression evaluating to an array

behavior: Useful when the function name or arguments must be constructed dynamically.
Arguments in $args are evaluated before the function is called.

examples.description: Call built-in joinStr with static args
Dynamic $args from scope

$switch.description: Pattern matching — evaluate an expression and select a branch by matching its string representation against keys.

parameters.$switch: Expression whose result (stringified) is matched against the object keys
parameters.$default: Optional fallback value if no key matches

behavior: The expression result is converted to a string and matched against the keys.
Returns the value of the matching key, or $default if provided, or null.

examples.description: Match computed value against string keys
Use $default for fallback
Returns null when no match and no $default

joinStr.description: Join array elements into a string with the given separator.

splitStr.description: Split a string by a regex pattern. Optional limit controls max number of splits. Null input returns [""].

substr.description: Extract a substring from start index to optional end index.

replace.description: Replace all occurrences matching the regex pattern. Null/empty input returns empty string.

toLowerCase.description: Convert string to lowercase. Null input returns empty string.

toUpperCase.description: Convert string to uppercase. Null input returns empty string.

capitalize.description: Capitalize first letter, lowercase the rest. Null input returns empty string.

str.description: Convert any value to its string representation. Keywords are converted to their name (without colon).

toString.description: Alias for str. Convert any value to string.

len.description: Return the count of elements in an array, characters in a string, or entries in a map.

uniq.description: Return array with duplicate values removed, preserving order.

flatten.description: Flatten nested arrays into a single-level array.

randNth.description: Return a random element from the array.

groupBy.description: Group array elements by the result of applying a function to each element.

merge.description: Merge multiple maps together. Later maps override earlier keys.

assoc.description: Return a new map with the given key set to the given value.

toInt.description: Parse a string or number as an integer.

toDec.description: Parse a string or number as a decimal (float).

toKeyword.description: Convert a string to a keyword (Clojure keyword type).

abs.description: Return the absolute value of a number.

range.signature: range(end) or range(start, end) or range(start, end, step)
range.description: Generate a sequence of numbers. Same semantics as Clojure's range.

now.description: Return the current date/time as an ISO-8601 string.

daysInMonth.description: Return the number of days in the given month/year. Handles leap years correctly.

dropBlanks.description: Recursively remove null values and empty collections from nested data structures. Removes map entries with null values, filters nulls from arrays, and drops empty sub-structures left after removal.

hash.description: Compute a hash value for the input.

println.description: Print a value to the console (for debugging). Returns the value.

discard-map-when-everything-evaluated-to.description: When enabled, if all dynamically-evaluated values in a map resolve to null, the entire map is discarded (returns null). Static values alone do not prevent discard. Maps containing 'false' values are preserved.

example.note: Even though bar=42 and x=12, y=24 are static, the single dynamic value z evaluated to null, so the entire root map is discarded.

counter_example.description: false values are not treated as null

data_types.description: Text values, quoted with single or double quotes in expressions
Integers and floating-point numbers. Arithmetic follows standard precedence.
true or false. Strict comparison: true != "True".
Null/nil value. Missing paths resolve to null.
Ordered collection. Supports indexing, wildcards, and iteration.
Key-value map. Supports dot-path navigation, wildcards, and iteration.

template_structure.overview: A Jute template is a JSON or YAML document. Any string value starting with '$ ' (dollar-space) is treated as an expression and evaluated against the input scope. Objects with directive keys ($if, $map, $let, $reduce, $fn, $call, $switch) are control structures. All other values pass through unchanged.
rules: Expressions must start with '$ ' (dollar sign followed by a space).
Directive keys start with '$' and are reserved: $if, $then, $else, $map, $as, $body, $reduce, $start, $from, $let, $fn, $name, $call, $args, $switch, $default.
Static values (strings not starting with '$ ', numbers, booleans, null) are returned as-is.
Arrays in templates are evaluated element-by-element.
Objects in templates are evaluated key-by-key, with expression values resolved.

template_examples.description: Using $let for intermediate computation and $reduce for aggregation
